s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of low back and abdominal pain with a retroperitoneal mass and hormonal abnormalities
key_facts: Active tobacco, alcohol, and marijuana use
Family history of prostate cancer, melanoma, and colon cancer
CT abdomen/pelvis showed a large right suprarenal retroperitoneal hemorrhagic mass
MRI adrenal protocol confirmed the right adrenal hemorrhagic mass
Numerous pulmonary nodules on chest CT

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of low back and abdominal pain with a retroperitoneal mass and hormonal abnormalities
key_facts: Active tobacco, alcohol, and marijuana use
Family history of prostate cancer, melanoma, and colon cancer
CT abdomen/pelvis showed a large right suprarenal retroperitoneal hemorrhagic mass
MRI adrenal protocol confirmed the right adrenal hemorrhagic mass
Numerous pulmonary nodules on chest CT

shortlist.label: Choriocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated beta-hCG levels and poorly differentiated tumor on pathology

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: High total metanephrine and normetanephrine levels

shortlist.label: Germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated beta-hCG levels and testicular ultrasound showed no neoplasm

shortlist.label: Ectopic beta-hCG producing tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated beta-hCG levels and no testicular neoplasm found

raw.rationale: Elevated serum β-hCG levels, which increased on repeat testing, and the presence of a poorly differentiated tumor with immunostaining positive for β-hCG, are key evidence supporting this diagnosis

rejected.label: Adrenal cortical carcinoma
rejected.why: While the mass is located near the adrenal gland, the tumor's characteristics and markers, especially the high β-hCG levels, do not align with adrenal cortical carcinoma

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: Although total metanephrine and normetanephrine are elevated, the primary findings of high β-hCG and the specific tumor markers do not support pheochromocytoma

rejected.label: Germ cell tumor
rejected.why: Testicular ultrasound showed no neoplasm, and while germ cell tumors can produce β-hCG, the absence of a testicular source and specific pathology findings point away from this diagnosis

rejected.label: Ectopic beta-hCG producing tumor
rejected.why: While the high β-hCG levels could suggest an ectopic source, the specific pathology and immunohistochemistry results, including the tumor's characteristics, more strongly support choriocarcinoma
